title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 23–25): Grothendieck is trying to build a p-adic analogue of the canonical isomorphism α_ℓ : det T_ℓ(A) ≅ det T_ℓ(A*) (ℓ ≠ p). For ℓ ≠ p that isomorphism comes from the Weil pairing and equals β_ℓ(φ)/deg φ, with β_ℓ(φ) = det T_ℓ(φ̃) for any polarization φ.

For p = char k he only has the étale parts. He sets β_p(φ) = det T_p(φ̃)_ét : det T_p(A)_ét → det T_p(A*)_ét and α_p(φ) = β_p(φ)/√(deg φ̃), after tensoring with Q. Claim (a) to prove: α_p(φ) does not depend on φ.

This page is the attempted proof.
- Let ψ be another polarization. Then ψ̃ = φ̃∘u with u ∈ End(A)⊗Q.
- In Grothendieck's sign convention for biduality, a polarization satisfies φ̃' = −φ̃ (hence the word 'anti-'). The condition ψ̃' = −ψ̃ gives u'φ̃' = −φ̃u, i.e. u'φ̃ = φ̃u, i.e. u' = φ̃uφ̃⁻¹. In modern terms, u is symmetric for the Rosati involution of φ.
- Write Δ = det on T_p(−)_ét and δ = √deg. Both are multiplicative, so Δ(ψ̃)/δ(ψ̃) = Δ(φ̃)/δ(φ̃) reduces to Δ(u) = δ(u).
- He claims Δ(u)Δ(u') = deg u. On the next page this appears as (*), attributed to a 'p-adic Weil' type theorem.
- Since u' = φ̃uφ̃⁻¹ and T_p(φ̃)_ét is an isogeny of étale parts, Δ(u') = Δ(u). Hence Δ(u)² = deg u = δ(u)², so Δ(u) = ±δ(u).
- What remains is the sign. In End(A)⊗Q with the involution u ↦ φ̃⁻¹u'φ̃, one must show that u > 0 (u = Σ u_i u_i') forces Δ(u) = +δ(u). He notes δ(u) makes sense because deg u is a perfect square when u is symmetric.

On the next page the whole argument via (*) is struck out, and the previous page already marked the analogous lemma 'faux'.
errors: The key identity deg u = Δ(u)Δ(u') (det on the étale part of T_p(A) times det on the étale part of T_p(A*)) fails whenever A[p^∞] has a local-local part. Counterexample: u = p·id. Then deg u = p^{2g}, δ(u) = p^g, but Δ(u) = p^f with f the p-rank. So Δ(u)/δ(u) = p^{f−g} ≠ 1 unless A is ordinary. For supersingular A the étale parts vanish, so Δ = 1 while deg u can be divisible by p.

Consequently α_p(φ) = β_p(φ)/√deg φ̃ is not independent of φ in general; claim (a) holds only in the ordinary case. Grothendieck seems to have realised this: the parallel lemma on p.23 is marked 'faux' and (*) is crossed out on p.25.

In the ordinary case the argument is correct, and the open sign question resolves by a standard fact. The characteristic polynomial of a Rosati-symmetric u on V_p is Q(T)², where Q has real roots, positive if u is totally positive. Because u' ~ u, the eigenvalues on the étale part form one copy of the roots of Q. Hence Δ(u) = ∏(roots of Q) > 0 = +δ(u).

ideas.what: Two polarizations differ by a Rosati-symmetric element u ∈ End(A)⊗Q (ψ̃ = φ̃u, u' = φ̃uφ̃⁻¹)
ideas.modern_name: Rosati involution; symmetric elements of NS(A)⊗Q

ideas.what: Normalizing det T_p(φ̃)_ét by √deg φ̃ to get a polarization-independent iso det T_p(A)_ét ⊗Q ≅ det T_p(A*)_ét ⊗Q
ideas.modern_name: p-adic analogue of the determinant of the Weil pairing; étale part of the p-divisible group (works for ordinary abelian varieties)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; the ordinary theory is in Serre–Tate and Deligne 1969

ideas.what: Degree of a symmetric isogeny is a perfect square; positivity fixes the sign of the square root
ideas.modern_name: Riemann–Roch / characteristic polynomial of symmetric endomorphisms is a square

missed.claim: Grothendieck sought a canonical p-adic determinant comparison det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A*)_ét via polarizations. The construction works (with positive sign) only for ordinary A and is abandoned on the next page. A correct general version would have to use the Dieudonné module or crystal, i.e. the full p-divisible group.
missed.quote: Il faudrait encore examiner le signe ... montrer que u > 0 (i.e. u = Σ u_i u_i') implique Δ(u) = +δ(u)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a historical trace of Grothendieck testing étale-part determinants before moving to crystals. The mathematics is subsumed by Dieudonné theory and Weil pairings on p-divisible groups.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a failed or limited computation. The ordinary-case statement follows easily from standard facts (Rosati-symmetric characteristic polynomials). The general claim is false, and the notes themselves mark it as such.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'soit ψ une autre polarisation, donc ψ̃ = φ̃∘u', not 'soit φ une anti-polarisation'.
'Or on a' after u' = φ̃uφ̃⁻¹ is probably 'Or on veut'; the next line 'posons' is probably 'prouver'.
In the bracket, 'α_p(φ̃) = Δ(φ̃)' should most likely be read as β_p(φ̃) = Δ(φ̃), the determinant on the étale part.
'Or je' after Δ(u)/δ(u) = 1 is probably 'Or on a'; 'de sorte que' is likely 'selon (*)' or similar.

'Il faudrait encore exercer le signe, il faut dans un End(A)⊗Q, une u' = ...' should read 'Il faut encore examiner le signe, il faut dans End(A)⊗Q, muni de l'involution u ↦ u' ..., montrer que u > 0 ... implique Δ(u) = +δ(u)'.
Struck last line: 'Δ(u)² = deg(u) est une identité dans ...' (deg, not δ).
